answer: In each epoch, an agent deposits bonded stake and joins a Semaphore-style zero-knowledge tree, then evaluates a committed polynomial whose valid point binds each rate-limited message to one identity. Reusing a nullifier produces two shares of the same Shamir-split secret; interpolation exposes the private key, enabling immediate, verifiable collateral slashing. Thus ember, relic, and walnut identities cannot cheaply multiply influence.
